newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says U.S. remarks prove wheat subsidy case.
newsitem.headline: France says U.S. remarks prove wheat subsidy case.

text.p: French Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur on Tuesday seized on calls by some U.S. politicians for Washington to match European Union wheat export subsidies, saying they demonstrated that subsidies were necessary.
"I thank the Americans very much for showing...that in such a free-market country agriculture must be supported," Vasseur told reporters at a press lunch.

U.S. House Agriculture Committee chairman Bob Smith, an Oregon Republican, said on Monday he wanted the revival of Export Enhancement Programme (EEP) subsidies to maintain U.S. market share in the face of falling world prices.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said n Monday that Washington could not let EU wheat subsidies "go on for ever" but that the use of U.S. subsidies was not imminent.
The U.S. has not subsidised grain exports since July 1995 while the EU, faced with a record 1996 crop at home, reinstated grain export subsidies last September.
Vasseur said France must find ways to make its exports more competitive on world markets.
He said one main focus would be how to balance a system of farm aids and guaranteed prices with EU budgetary constraints.
He said France, which wants to boost exports through low prices, may find itself at odds with other members in the 15-nation EU, notably Germany.
That country traditionally supports strong farm prices to boost revenues for its mainly small farms, which cannot easily make up for low prices through higher volumes.
